#Inventory

#Internal caches (remove by making the path fast; product caches kept)

Kept, a product: the HTTP cache (src/httpcache), the back/forward cache (browser/bfcache.odin), compiled scripts on disk (js/cache.odin), compiled Wasm modules (wasm/module_cache.odin), the Cache API (page/cache_store.odin): each saves the network or a compiler's work across navigations and starts, which no faster path can. GPU residency, not caches: the glyph atlas (font/raster.odin:71), Slug glyph data (font/slug_cache.odin:44), image textures (browser/images_shell.odin:70), retained pictures (browser/compositor.odin:129, with its memory budget). Not a cache either: the table of a style pass that gives elements with the same inputs the same computed style (style/share.odin, round 4): it holds the values that pass made and goes with it, nothing in it is invalidated; nor the families of the walk that share matching between alike elements (style/sibling_match.odin, round 5): what the pass matched for the first of a kind, dropped when the walk leaves that family; nor the pairs of records a chunk of the layout journal's comparison has compared (style/journal.odin, round 8), which live while that chunk is compared.

#Heap lists per call on hot paths

style/timeline.odin:429-432,468 (an Element_Anim and three dynamic arrays for each element that declares a transition, on every full pass); browser/compositor.odin:322 (compute_floors: one heap array per group per rebuild) and :532 (node_items_make: one per node); the window thread's and the thread pool's temporary arenas, which give back what outgrew their first block after each frame or job (NtFreeVirtualMemory, 1 % of the window thread on nodes10k; the pool's are src/host's). Most of layout and paint already use the temporary allocator or an arena.

  1. The script stage of DOM-heavy pages, what is left (nodes10k: 11.8 ms of a 17.7 ms frame; the browser's side 1.4 ms of it). In order of the engine's samples: the interpreter itself (interp_hot 17 % before round 15's 15 to 25 % on the loop's own instructions, call_native and the bridge 8 %; a DOM call costs 50 to 100 ns over the loop); the collection the DOM asks for (2.9 ms every 2 frames: the browser's Node_unpinAll, the prologue's walk of every wrapper with JS_IsUntouched for each, the finalizers' chain of calls, the sweep's frees, gc_drain); the browser's insertions (0.5 ms a frame by the browser's sampler: the insertion hooks 29 %, the journal 23 %, check_insert 9 %); the browser's factories (create_element, pool_insert_tagged copying a Node by value, the pin, the interface); making the wrappers (6 %). Texts are still copied to the heap and freed one by one (create_text, about 0.1 ms a frame). Measured and left: a flag per interface for the unforgeable members of its chain (round 7); the finalizers' skipped calls, the pre-sweep walks in one, the prologue's walk inlined, temp_reset in place (round 12); the hot loop as a procedure of its own (round 15: 8 % slower than inlined).
  2. Layout of DOM-heavy pages: the steps' own code (nodes10k: the window thread waits 3.1 ms a frame, the page thread's full pass: tree 0.96, layout 1.07, finish 0.32, display 0.37, bands 0.13 ms). Round 10 found the records' layout no gain, round 11 took the image search, the cut of the flow and the display item's padding. What the profile shows now, by cost: building the box tree (19 % of the page thread; place_element, and the layout threads' summaries of the styles); the block layout of the columns (34 %, no part above 0.11 ms in process: apply_shifts moving every box to its column, then the 2 500 items' own layout at about 150 ns each: a shorter path for an item whose paragraph came from the threads and whose style is its siblings' is what is left to try); finishing (finish itself 6 %); note_refresh_inputs (4.5 %: every display item and inline item read again after the list is made, which the shares making the list could note as they go); the bands (4.4 %).
  3. What a full style pass still costs per page (mutation_fullstyle, the style stage 0.75 ms in the browser, a pass 0.57 ms in process with seven threads since round 14, four fifths of that on the threads since round 9): on the style threads, matching (match_chain, the families of pages whose elements are each of their own kind: modern-css, p10k, matched in full as before) and the journal's comparison of the pairs that differ; on the window thread, the weights of the subtrees (0.07 ms, one walk since round 9: weights the DOM keeps would cost every insertion).
  4. The temporary arenas of the window thread and of the thread pool (src/host): emptied by zeroing what they held after each frame or job (mem_free_all and its memset are 6 to 12 % of some pool threads' samples on nodes10k), and given back past their first block. Allocations that need no zero (make of what is overwritten whole) are the gain there, not when the zeroing happens (round 5, item 5).
  5. The atlas lock and the word cache's 64 locks (toolkit): toolkit 0.64.0 took the atlas lock once per run of glyphs and a word cache hit under a shared lock (its docs/locks.md: 8 threads, a word's shape 442 -> 194 ns, a glyph's bitmap 120 -> 17 ns); what is left is measuring the page's text again before any per-thread front.

  7. The job queues of the blocking pool, the image decoders, the script compiler and the caches (the table above): measured first (round 3: a lock-free queue lost to the loop's mutex); a worker's ordered_remove(0) is a cost of its own.
  8. The profiler: correct the bias of samples taken in a system call.
  9. The interpreter, what is left after its loop (round 15): the full dispatch of interp_run for what the loop leaves (closures made, arguments, spreads, destructuring of iterables: the two cases of macro.js that did not gain are there), and native callbacks (sort, forEach: an interp_run activation each). A handler added to the loop must call nothing itself (interp_hot.odin's header says how).
  10. Pages loaded from the navigation (round 15, item 3; wrentool bench perf -Only p10k_nav,nav_...): the first realm of a process (the engine's compiled code read from the disk cache and its whole file hashed for the HMAC on the window thread, 10 to 15 ms, then instantiated: a page's first inline script waits 50 to 65 ms) could be read ahead, off the window thread, when the process starts; the first paint of text makes the system's font factory and color glyph tables on the window thread (text.html: first paint 27 to 66 ms after its load); a remote stats walks every process of the machine for its own thread count (20 to 45 ms).
